statement: Every prophet tended sheep; he tended sheep for the people of Makkah for a few qirats.
notes: Machine-checked against the dataset on 2026-10-03. Direct speech.

statement: At about twelve he travelled with Abu Talib in a trade caravan toward Syria.
alternatives: Age given as twelve, or twelve years and some months.

statement: The story of the monk Bahira recognising him on that journey exists but its chain was judged unsound by several hadith scholars; it is not narrated.
notes: The underlying report is grade D for narration: graded munkar (al-Albani, Ahmad Shakir) and da'if (Zubair Ali Zai) in the dataset, though at-Tirmidhi called it hasan gharib. Reviewer to confirm the wording is fair.

statement: The Fijar war between Quraysh with Kinanah and Qays Aylan was fought in the sacred months; he was present with his uncles as a youth and handed them arrows.
alternatives: His age is given as fourteen, fifteen or twenty.

statement: After it, clans of Quraysh met in the house of Abdullah ibn Jud'an and pledged to stand with anyone wronged in Makkah until his right was restored: Hilf al-Fudul.
He later said he witnessed that pact, would not exchange it for red camels, and would answer if called to it in Islam.
notes: Reported by the Seerah historians; a similar wording about a pact witnessed in his youth is in Musnad Ahmad and graded sahih by some. Narrated as a report until the reviewer confirms a graded source and exact wording.

statement: He took no part in the idol worship of his people.
At Safa he asked Quraysh whether they would believe him if he warned of cavalry in the valley; they said yes, we have never found you saying anything but the truth.
Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan whether they had ever accused him of lying before his claim; Abu Sufyan said no.
notes: Reviewer to check the exact wording of the question in Bukhari 7.

statement: His people called him al-Amin, the Trustworthy.
He had no inherited wealth; Khadijah, a merchant of Makkah, hired men to trade with her goods.
